minutes.headline: Finance Committee previewed FY24 budget season, approved corrected October minutes 5-0, and tabled November minutes.
minutes.summary: The committee welcomed a new sixth member and heard the town manager's budget priorities update: state aid level funded until the new governor's proposal, health insurance and retirement pressures, and staffing requests. It reviewed the goals and procedures document for department heads, discussed inviting the legislative delegation, and reassigned committee liaisons. It approved corrected October 13 minutes by roll call and held the November minutes for lack of review.

public_comment.topic: A speaker announced that lakefront properties on several lakes received tax bills with large assessment increases, and described a planned meeting for affected owners and the next Select Board meeting with the assessor.

votes.motion: Approve the October 13, 2022 minutes as amended to add that a motion was made, seconded and unanimous
votes.outcome: passed unanimously on roll call (five members voting aye, as heard)

budget_items.what_was_said: Target budget has local receipts rising to match the same amount of added spending on pavement management.
State aid is level funded until the governor's proposal, due by early March.
The renewal rate used for budgeting is higher than expected to be final, with the actual rate expected between.
Liability and workers comp estimated up; retirement assessment received as an increase.
Select board must act on an additional retiree COLA, retroactive to July 1; impact is being requested.
Requests include ADA improvements, tree removal, drainage, cemetery, IT, a kennel and library programming; cemetery items below capital threshold.
Non-union salary impact would be funded through the salary reserve appropriation.
The school budget request was reported as increasing around three to three and a half percent; school committee has not voted.

budget_items.what_was_said: Registration cost compared with the committee's meetings fund balance, enough for about one and seven eighths attendees.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard the town manager's FY24 budget priorities, with state aid level funded until the governor's proposal, due by early March.
The committee approved the corrected October 13 minutes by roll call and held the November minutes for lack of review, without a vote.
Health insurance, liability, workers comp and retirement costs were reported rising, along with a pending retiree COLA the Select Board must act on.
The school department's budget request was reported as rising, but the school committee has not voted on it.
The capital plan and financial forecast presentation was pushed to January 26, and the chair will follow up on a separate meeting with the legislative delegation.

why_it_matters: The FY24 budget is still being assembled: state aid is a placeholder until the governor's proposal, and the school request is unvoted, so the figures that set next year's tax bill can still move.
A speaker raised large assessment increases on lakefront properties at public comment; assessments feed the tax bill, and the committee may take the topic up on January 26.
watch_next: January 26 meeting: capital plan and financial forecast presentation, and a possible assessments discussion.
The governor's budget proposal, due by early March, which replaces the level-funded state aid assumption.
